nodes.name: Interfacial Trapping Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The synthetic route utilizes an aqueous two-phase system (ATPS) composed of immiscible benzaldehyde and oleic acid solvents, offering a green, controllable, and waste-minimizing synthetic environment. In this system, H₂PtCl₆, dissolved in benzaldehyde provides [PtCl₆]²⁻ precursors, while Cs₂CO₃, dissolved in oleic acid, supplies Cs⁺ ions. The Cs₂PtCl₆ crystallization occurs spontaneously at the liquid-liquid interface, where the minimization of interfacial free energy and mass transfer dynamics drive the formation of small, well-defined crystals under ambient conditions.
nodes.source_text: A key innovation... development of an room-temperature interfacial trapping method to synthesize Cs₂PtCl₆ materials... The synthetic route, depicted in Scheme 1a, utilizes an aqueous two-phase system (ATPS) composed of immiscible benzaldehyde and oleic acid solvents

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: For a fair comparison, a control sample of Cs₂PtCl₆ was also synthesized using a conventional hydrothermal method, involving high-temperature treatment of precursors in an acidic aqueous solution (see Scheme 1b and Supporting Information for detail).
nodes.source_text: we applied a ubiquitous hydrothermal method to prepare perovskite Cs₂PtCl₆ (H), where (H) denotes the requirement of high temperature (>150°C)... a control sample of Cs₂PtCl₆ was also synthesized using a conventional hydrothermal method

nodes.name: MXene Compositing
nodes.procedure: Both interfacially synthesized (Cs₂PtCl₆) and hydrothermally derived (Cs₂PtCl₆(H)) were composited with delaminated V₄C₃Tₓ MXene, where the proposed mechanism incorporates [PtCl₆]²⁻ octahedra inset into the surface of V₄C₃Tₓ MXene, forming hybrid heterostructures Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ.
nodes.source_text: Both interfacially synthesized (Cs₂PtCl₆) and hydrothermally derived (Cs₂PtCl₆ H)) were composited with delaminated V₄C₃Tₓ MXene

nodes.name: Nb4C3Tx Compositing

nodes.source_text: Using the same synthetic protocol as preparing Cs₂PtCl₆(L)@V₄C₃Tₓ Cs₂PtCl₆ deposited on Nb₄C₃Tₓ and Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXenes

nodes.description: HER LSV performance in 0.5 M H₂SO₄
nodes.source_text: As shown in the polarization curves (Figure 2a), the Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃T_X heterostructure exhibits substantially higher HER activity in acidic media, achieving a remarkably low overpotential of only 39 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² ... the V₄C₃T_X -based composite demonstrated the lowest Tafel slope of 54.5 mV dec⁻¹
compared to the hydrothermal counterpart composite with an overpotential 138 mV
the catalyst also exhibits considerable activity in 1 M KOH with an overpotential of 48 mV
108.7 mV dec⁻¹ for the Nb₄C₃T_x -based composite
260.2 mV dec⁻¹ for the Ti₃C₂T_x -based system in acidic media
The obtained Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃T_{(OH)} exhibited excellent HER performance with an overpotential of 47 mV

nodes.source_text: the Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃T_X composite demonstrates excellent UOR activity characterized by a low onset potential and high current density (Figure 2h,i)

nodes.description: HER stability via cyclic voltammetry in 0.5 M H₂SO₄
nodes.source_text: the catalyst retained over 95% of its original current density after 1000 cycles of HER in 0.5 M H₂SO₄

The optimal composite (10 wt% Cs₂PtCl₆) displayed the highest ECSA of 2801.6 cm² ... exhibited a TOF of 51.4 s⁻¹, with a corresponding ECSA of 2801.6 cm², jECSA of 0.0357 mA cm⁻², and a high density of active sites (2.16×10¹² sites cm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image of Cs₂PtCl₆ particles synthesized via interfacial trapping shows size distribution ≈50-200 nm in diameter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a reveals the SEM image of the Cs₂PtCl₆ particles synthesized via the interfacial trapping method. The size distribution is calculated to be ≈50-200 nm in diameter.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms fine structural features of Cs₂PtCl₆ particles from interfacial trapping; Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ shows particle size reduction to ≈5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The seamless evolution of Cs₂PtCl₆ via the interfacial trapping method is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), which shows the fine structural features of Cs₂PtCl₆ particles (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows distinct interface between Cs₂PtCl₆ and V₄C₃Tₓ MXene indicating strong physical contact.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A distinct interface between Cs₂PtCl₆ and V₄C₃Tₓ MXene is observed in the HRTEM image (Figure 1f), indicating strong physical contact that facilitates charge transfer.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows even distribution of Cs, Pt, Cl, and V throughout Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping through energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) provides further confirmation of structural homogeneity of Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ heterostructure. EDS maps (Figure 1i-l) demonstrate an even and continuous distribution of Cs, Pt, and Cl elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Cs₂PtCl₆, Cs₂PtCl₆(H), and Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ match cubic Fm3m space group with characteristic peaks of both components preserved.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction patterns of both Cs₂PtCl₆ and Cs₂PtCl₆(H) closely matched the standard data reported for the cubic Fm3m space group... characteristic peaks of Cs₂PtCl₆ and V₄C₃TₓMXene were clearly observed (Figure 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows rightward shift to higher binding energies in Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ; Cs 3d₅/₂ and Cs 3d₃/₂ at 726 and 739 eV; Pt 4f shows positive shift indicating interfacial charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A noticeable shift toward higher binding energies (rightward shift) was observed in the Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ... Cs 3d₅/₂ and Cs 3d₃/₂ located at 726 and 739 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectrum of Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ shows well-resolved increased signal intensity attributed to interfacial defect states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR spectrum of the Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ heterostructure (Figure S11) exhibits a well-resolved and significantly increased signal intensity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Zeta potential of Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ is -18.7 mV initially, shifts to -34.5 mV after HER and -27.2 mV after UOR.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Initially, the Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ composite exhibited a zeta potential of -18.7 mV... After prolonged HER operation, this shifted significantly to -34.5 mV.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV measurements at varying scan rates used to extract double-layer capacitance (Cdl) for ECSA estimation. The optimal 10 wt% Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ composite displayed the highest ECSA of 2801.6 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: CV measurements at varying scan rates (Figure S9) were used to extract double-layer capacitance (Cdl), which in turn was used to estimate the ECSA... The optimal composite (10 wt% Cs₂PtCl₆) displayed the highest ECSA of 2801.6 cm².

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows significantly reduced charge transfer resistance (Rct) for Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ compared to other MXene composites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nyquist plots (Figure S8a) reveal that the interfacially engineered Cs₂PtCl₆@V₄C₃Tₓ exhibits a significantly reduced charge transfer resistance (Rct).
